findings.rationale: Local performance is badly degraded: AUC 0.60 (z=-6.7), ECE 0.142 (z=+10.9), CITL -0.134 (z=-10.2) and observed prevalence 0.289 against a federation norm near 0.15, so the labels look inflated with positives. Per-round prevalence is already about 0.26 in round 1, so the fault is present from the start. Subgroup O/E is about 1.8-2.0 in both sex groups, i.e. positives are over-recorded across the board, not under-recorded in one subgroup. The update is anomalous (mean cos -0.74, z=-9.1; median norm ratio 5.67, z=+7.7), which is what a client training on wrong labels produces. Local data is abnormal, so this is label_noise rather than poisoning.

Subgroup O/E is about 1.7-1.8 in both sex groups and about 2.4 in income group 6, so positives are over-recorded rather than under-recorded in a single subgroup. The update is anomalous (mean cos -0.74, z=-9.1; median norm ratio 4.95, z=+7.3). Local data is abnormal, so this is label_noise rather than poisoning.

Local AUC is 0.60 (z=-6.9), ECE 0.119 (z=+8.5), CITL -0.110 (z=-8.5) and prevalence 0.283 versus a federation norm near 0.15, so the labels are inflated with positives. Prevalence is elevated from round 1 (0.312) onward. Subgroup O/E is about 1.6-1.8 in both sex groups and 1.8 in income group 5, so the over-recording is general rather than confined to one subgroup. The update is anomalous (mean cos -0.68, z=-8.7; median norm ratio 4.27, z=+6.7). Local data is abnormal, so this is label_noise rather than poisoning.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then followed up on the suspicious clients with per-round drift for NE, OH and WI. Three clients stand out consistently: NE, OH and WI. Each has AUC about 0.6, CITL about -0.11 to -0.13, observed prevalence about 0.28-0.29 against a federation norm near 0.15, and updates pointing against the median with norm ratios around 4-6. Their over-recording of positives is spread across all sex, age and income groups, and the miscalibration is present from round 1. That pattern fits label noise (flipped labels), not subgroup_bias or prevalence_shift (AUC is normal there), and local data is abnormal, so I did not call it poisoning. Not reported: GU (small client, 708 records; update-norm z=+4.5 and mean-cos z=-3.2 with normal local performance, below the threshold), plus scattered feature-outlier and drift-onset flags on small clients (AL, NV, PR, VI, IL, GU), which are within the expected noise range and were not confirmed. No missing_artefact signature (no sentinel-like tail percentiles). Attribution churn (explanation_instability) was not screened because the budget ran out. Budget was fully spent (20.0 of 20.0).
